proposedTopics.title: Data Structures & Algorithms
proposedTopics.description: Root of the DSA learning path. Structure: NeetCode roadmap category order, each split into reviewable sub-patterns (the actual scheduling unit), each with curated problems from NeetCode 150 / Blind 75. Prereq edges follow real conceptual dependency, not just roadmap position. Study one sub-pattern at a time; drill into individual problems only when reviewing that sub-pattern.

proposedTopics.title: Arrays & Hashing
proposedTopics.description: Foundation category: hash-based lookup and array manipulation underlie most other patterns. No DSA prereqs — entry point.

proposedTopics.title: Hashing fundamentals
proposedTopics.description: Use a hash set/map to turn an O(n) membership or lookup check into O(1). Recognize: "have I seen this before", "does X exist", frequency counts.

proposedTopics.title: Two Sum / complement lookup
proposedTopics.description: For each element, check whether its complement (target - x) was already seen; store as you go instead of nested-looping. Recognize: "pair that sums/multiplies to X", single pass with a map.

proposedTopics.title: Grouping by key
proposedTopics.description: Bucket elements by a derived key (sorted string, character-count signature) into a hash map of lists. Recognize: "group these into categories", anagram/shape clustering.

proposedTopics.title: Prefix sums
proposedTopics.description: Precompute running sums so any range sum is O(1) via subtraction; combine with a hash map of seen prefix sums for subarray-sum problems. Recognize: repeated range-sum queries, "subarray with sum equal to X".

proposedTopics.title: Sorting-based array tricks
proposedTopics.description: Sort first to unlock two-pointer scans, deduplication, or greedy choices that only work on ordered data. Recognize: problem becomes easy once sorted, needs original-vs-sorted comparison.

proposedPrompts.promptText: When do you reach for a hash set/map as the core of a solution? Name the problem-statement signals, and the classic pitfall.
proposedPrompts.answerHint: Signals: "have I seen this before", "does X exist", frequency counting, any O(n^2) membership scan you can make O(n). Pitfall: hashing mutable/unnormalized keys (forgetting to sort or canonicalize the thing you look up). Related: Top K Frequent Elements builds a frequency map first.

proposedPrompts.promptText: Write a frequency counter in your language of choice: given an array, build a map value -> count in one pass, then use it to find any value appearing exactly twice.
proposedPrompts.answerHint: One loop, map.get(x) defaulting to 0 then +1; second loop (or the same one) checks counts. Invariant: after i iterations the map holds exact counts for the first i elements.

proposedPrompts.promptText: Solve: Contains Duplicate (Easy) — return true if any value appears at least twice in the array.
proposedPrompts.answerHint: Set of seen values; return true the moment insertion finds the value already present.

proposedPrompts.promptText: Solve: Valid Anagram (Easy) — given two strings, return true if one is an anagram of the other.
proposedPrompts.answerHint: Character-frequency map of s, decrement over t; all zeros means anagram (or compare two count maps).

proposedPrompts.promptText: Solve: Longest Consecutive Sequence (Medium) — length of the longest run of consecutive integers in an unsorted array, in O(n).
proposedPrompts.answerHint: Hash-set all values; only start counting from numbers whose predecessor (x-1) is absent — each element is visited at most twice.

proposedPrompts.promptText: When do you reach for the complement-lookup pattern? Name the problem-statement signals, and the classic pitfall.
proposedPrompts.answerHint: Signals: "pair summing/multiplying to X", single unsorted pass where sorting would cost the indices. Pitfall: inserting the current element BEFORE checking its complement (breaks on target = 2x). Related: Two Sum II (sorted input) belongs to opposite-direction pointers; Subarray Sum Equals K is the same idea on prefix sums.

proposedPrompts.promptText: Write the single-pass complement lookup in your language of choice: given an array and target, return the indices of a pair summing to target.
proposedPrompts.answerHint: Map value -> index built as you scan; check map for (target - x) before inserting x. Invariant: map only ever holds elements strictly left of the cursor.

proposedPrompts.promptText: Solve: Two Sum (Easy) — indices of the two numbers adding to target, one valid answer guaranteed.
proposedPrompts.answerHint: Check seen-map for complement, then store current value -> index.

proposedPrompts.promptText: Solve: 4Sum II (Medium) — count tuples (i,j,k,l) across four arrays with A[i]+B[j]+C[k]+D[l] == 0.
proposedPrompts.answerHint: Split into halves: map of all A+B sums with counts, then look up -(C+D) — complement lookup on pair-sums, O(n^2).

proposedPrompts.promptText: When do you reach for grouping-by-derived-key? Name the problem-statement signals, and the classic pitfall.
proposedPrompts.answerHint: Signals: "group/cluster these", items equivalent under a canonical form (sorted string, count signature, normalized shape). Pitfall: a non-canonical key (grouping anagrams by first letter) or an ambiguous string join (use a delimiter that can't appear in the data). Related: Group Shifted Strings uses a shift-invariant signature.

proposedPrompts.promptText: Write the bucket-by-key loop in your language of choice: given a list of strings, group them into lists of mutual anagrams.
proposedPrompts.answerHint: key = sorted(word) (or 26-count signature stringified); map key -> list, push each word, return the map's values.

proposedPrompts.promptText: Solve: Group Anagrams (Medium) — group a list of strings into anagram clusters.
proposedPrompts.answerHint: Sorted string (or char-count tuple) as the bucket key; one pass.

proposedPrompts.promptText: Solve: Encode and Decode Strings (Medium) — design encode(list of strings) -> string and decode(string) -> list that round-trip any input.
proposedPrompts.answerHint: Length-prefix each string (e.g. "4#word") — delimiters alone can't work because any character may appear in the data.

proposedPrompts.promptText: When do you reach for prefix sums? Name the problem-statement signals, and the classic pitfall.
proposedPrompts.answerHint: Signals: repeated range-sum queries, "subarray with sum X", running totals compared across positions. Pitfall: forgetting the empty prefix (seed the map with {0: 1}) — it's what lets a subarray starting at index 0 count.

proposedPrompts.promptText: Write the prefix-sum setup in your language of choice: build the prefix array for nums, then answer sum(i..j) queries in O(1).
proposedPrompts.answerHint: prefix has length n+1 with prefix[0]=0, prefix[k]=prefix[k-1]+nums[k-1]; sum(i..j) = prefix[j+1]-prefix[i].

proposedPrompts.promptText: Solve: Range Sum Query - Immutable (Easy) — preprocess an array to answer sumRange(i, j) calls in O(1).
proposedPrompts.answerHint: Length n+1 prefix array; subtraction answers each query.

proposedPrompts.promptText: Solve: Subarray Sum Equals K (Medium) — count subarrays summing to exactly k.
proposedPrompts.answerHint: Running sum + map of seen prefix-sum counts; at each step add count of (running - k). Seed {0: 1}.

proposedPrompts.promptText: Solve: Product of Array Except Self (Medium) — output[i] = product of all elements except nums[i], no division, O(n).
proposedPrompts.answerHint: Prefix products left-to-right, then a right-to-left running suffix product multiplied in — prefix idea with * instead of +.

proposedPrompts.promptText: When is "sort it first" the unlocking move? Name the problem-statement signals, and the classic pitfall.
proposedPrompts.answerHint: Signals: pairing/adjacency becomes meaningful once ordered, dedup, greedy picks by size/deadline, original-vs-sorted comparison. Pitfall: sorting away information you still need (original indices — copy or argsort first). Related: Sort Colors (three-way partitioning), Kth Largest (heap/quickselect), Meeting Rooms and Merge Intervals (intervals category).

proposedPrompts.promptText: Solve: Merge Sorted Array (Easy) — merge nums2 into nums1 in place, where nums1 has trailing space for the result.
proposedPrompts.answerHint: Fill from the BACK (largest first) with two read pointers — writing from the front overwrites unread values.

proposedPrompts.promptText: Solve: Largest Number (Medium) — arrange non-negative integers to form the largest possible number (as a string).
proposedPrompts.answerHint: Sort with the custom comparator: a before b iff concat(a,b) > concat(b,a). Watch the all-zeros case ("00" -> "0").
